messages:
sarah (partnerships): Heads up — ORION sent a manifest update. They put ~60% of reserved racks for the Acme Dedicated pilot on hold. ETA moved from 2025-05-08 -> 2025-05-22. This will impact the Q2 customer onboarding window. Need immediate allocation and comms plan.

orion-contact (vendor): FYI — export hold due to EU customs paperwork mismatch. We can split into two shipments: 40% ships next week (air), remainder on May 22 (sea). SKU-level manifest: `MAN-ORION-5582`. We can provide certificates by EOD.

ine-bot (logistics-bot): Received manifest `MAN-ORION-5582`. Current reservation mapping: 12 racks reserved for Acme-Pilot (cust-id: ACME-009). Proposed partial fulfil: 5 racks (air) on 2025-04-30, 7 racks (sea) on 2025-05-22.

mike (supply-chain): @sarah @raj this changes our capacity allocation. If we push 5 racks early, we can keep the pilot's canary but not full throughput. We should decide who gets the early slots (Acme vs internal e2e).

raj (sales): Customer expectation was full dedicated cluster by May 10. Acme will be upset if we drop to 40%. We need a comms plan that offers either partial access or temporary Hosted fallback. Can we offer a Hosted burst for the missing capacity?

ine-bot (logistics-bot): Hosted fallback available in EU region with warm pool — capacity estimate: 50-70% of missing QPS for short term. Cost delta approx +18% for peak traffic.

ana (legal): We need to check contract SLO language before promising Hosted fallback as a mitigation. If we advertise Dedicated commit and then shift, risk of breach. Let me review the Acme contract clause 4.2.

oliver (customer-success): If we do partial handover, we should prepare a short playbook for Acme: what features are limited, estimated performance, and expected dates for final racks. I can draft a 2-paragraph note once scope decided.

mike (supply-chain): Proposal: allocate the 5 early racks to Acme's canary nodes only (to validate integration). Keep 7 racks reserved for final cutover on 2025-05-22. If Acme needs more, offer Hosted burst until second shipment arrives.

raj (sales): Sounds reasonable. Two asks: 1) internal migration script readiness for partial->full cluster switch, 2) a cost estimate to present to Acme for Hosted burst (if accepted).

sarah (partnerships): Action items: 
- @mike: confirm which physical racks (IDs) are in the 5-rack air manifest and share serials (due: today EOD).
- @orion-contact: send customs certificates + airway bill for early shipment, and updated ETA for second shipment (due: 2 hours).
- @ana: quick contract read for SLO breach risk (due: 4 hours).
- @oliver: draft customer note for partial delivery scenario (due: by tomorrow 10am).
- @raj: prepare Hosted burst cost delta for missing capacity (due: 6 hours).

orion-contact (vendor): Acknowledged — sending airway bill + certificates now. Early shipment rack IDs: R-5582A, R-5582B, R-5582C, R-5582D, R-5582E. Sea shipment will list rest.

mike (supply-chain): Got rack IDs. I'm checking serials now. Small note — air freight will require additional customs broker fee (approx $3k).

ana (legal): Quick read: Acme contract has a mitigation clause allowing reasonable substitution if customer agrees in writing. We must get written consent before switching to Hosted fallback for committed Dedicated capacity.

raj (sales): I'll ping Acme engineering lead for an emergency sync once we have the airway bill + short proposed mitigation (oliver, can you draft that in parallel?).

oliver (customer-success): Drafting short note now. Will include: partial handover plan, what is limited, timeline for full cutover, ask for written approval of Hosted fallback.

mike (supply-chain): From serials check: 3 racks show slightly older firmware (v1.9.3) vs our fleet baseline (v2.0.0). Suggest we reserve 1 pre-staging slot for firmware bump before handing to Acme. That will add ~2 business days to the air plan unless we do remote flash during transit.

sarah (partnerships): Important tradeoff. Options: (A) remote flash during transit (requires vendor support) and ship on current schedule, (B) do pre-staging (delays handover), (C) push older racks to internal test and request vendor swap. Thoughts?

orion-contact (vendor): We can support remote flashing at our staging facility and confirm integrity checks before handoff. Need a signed waiver for remote operations on the units.

ana (legal): I'll add the waiver to the customer note template. Keep me looped in.

raj (sales): If remote flash is fast, Acme will prefer that over delay. I'll include it as our recommended option in the initial comms.

oliver (customer-success): Draft ready — short note attached (link): https://docs.internal/redwood/acme-partial-handback-draft — includes ask for written approval and waiver.

mike (supply-chain): Final note: confirm cost apportioning for extra broker fee + air vs sea variance. We should decide whether Redwood absorbs fees for pilot or passes to Acme. That will affect acceptance.

sarah (partnerships): Let's do a quick decision: Redwood absorbs customs broker fee for pilot goodwill; we pass marginal hosting delta to customer only if they choose Hosted burst. Everyone OK?

raj (sales): OK from sales — we'll frame Hosted burst as optional and billable. Redwood covers customs broker fee for pilot only.

ana (legal): Fine. I will caveat with standard 'pilot goodwill' clause.

sarah (partnerships): Great. Summary of next steps in thread: 
1) @orion-contact send docs (in flight).
2) @mike confirm serials + firmware plan.
3) @oliver & @raj coordinate customer comms and ask for written approval + waiver.
4) @ana finalize waiver language.
5) @sarah to run exec heads-up once airway bill confirmed.

Please react with :thumbsup: if you accept these assignments or reply with blockers.
